items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: although he certainly wouldn't have been considered as jazz oriented as somebody like Johnny Hodges or Hilton Jefferson or Happy Haddie Caldwell, anybody like that.

ctx.x: I don't think he ever did. He was a fantastic technician; absolutely fantastic, believe me. And he was much more jazz oriented than you know, than Rudy Wiedoeft, although he certainly wouldn't have been considered as jazz oriented as somebody like Johnny Hodges or Hilton Jefferson or Happy Haddie Caldwell, anybody like that.
What about a Boyd Centa? I mean he made a great number of records.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It seems to me that Hilton Jefferson and I were in the orchestra together.

ctx.x: Why don’t we move to your next association, I think major one, and that would be McKinney’s Cotton Pickers, which again was another instance of you sort of following Don Redmond, who had been musical director. How did you hook up with McKinney’s?

Well, I guess Bill McKinney had invited me to join the orchestra and wanted to know if I would come to Detroit, which I did. It seems to me that Hilton Jefferson and I were in the orchestra together. Were we? Gee, I don’t know what makes me think that.
I don’t think so, but it’s . . .
